title: Monitoring Models: Data Drift & Dataset Shift
summary: Models fail quietly when live data stops looking like training data. Learn the kinds of shift, and the two statistics most monitoring systems use to detect them: PSI and the Kolmogorov–Smirnov distance.
takeaways: Labels arrive late, but inputs arrive now. Comparing input distributions is your early warning.
PSI measures how far binned proportions moved. KS measures the largest gap between empirical CDFs.
Bin PSI on reference-data quantiles, and clip empty bins to a small epsilon to avoid log(0).
Thresholds (PSI 0.1 / 0.25) are rules of thumb, so tune alerts to your own data.

steps.label: Reference window
steps.detail: Snapshot each feature's distribution from training or a known-good period.

steps.label: Current window
steps.detail: Collect the same features from recent production traffic.

steps.label: Compute PSI + KS
steps.detail: Per feature: binned shift (PSI) and maximum CDF gap (KS).

steps.label: Compare thresholds
steps.detail: Flag features whose PSI crosses the alert threshold.

steps.label: Act
steps.detail: Investigate upstream data, retrain, or roll back, depending on which features moved.

terms.definition: Any change between the training and deployment data distributions.

The relationship between inputs and target, P(y|x), changes over time.
Population Stability Index: Σ (c − r)·ln(c/r) over bins of current and reference proportions.
The maximum absolute difference between two empirical cumulative distribution functions.
F(x) = fraction of sample values ≤ x.
